gap: No result ChatGPT got states that with LDAC and ANC both on, the makers' own figures fall to 5 h per charge for the Soundcore Liberty 4 NC (from a 10 h headline), 5.5 h for the CMF Buds 2 Plus (from 14 h) and 4.5 h for the Nothing Ear (3a) (from 10 h), or that Soundcore's own page says turning on LDAC drops the Liberty 4 NC out of multipoint.
standout_why: I checked against SoundGuys' best-under-$100 list (cited in every chat), the SoundGuys LDAC list (cited twice) and Skimwire (cited three times). SoundGuys under $100 gives battery tests (Liberty 4 NC 9 h 53 min with ANC on, CMF Buds 2 Plus 10 h 22 min with ANC off) but never says which codec was used. Only its CMF Clip Pro result says 'with LDAC on'. Skimwire repeats the AAC-based headlines (Liberty 4 NC 10 h / 50 h, CMF 61.5 h, EarFun 11 h / 52 h) and says nothing about LDAC versus AAC. The SoundGuys LDAC page says in general that 'you cannot use LDAC with Bluetooth multipoint', and one ChatGPT answer repeated that. So the multipoint point is partly covered, but no rival page puts LDAC-mode battery side by side across models.
decides: ChatGPT keeps picking the Liberty 4 NC for 'ANC and battery' using SoundGuys' roughly 10 h figure. The question is about LDAC, though, and Soundcore's own FAQ says LDAC plus ANC gives 5 h, half of that. That puts it level with the CMF Buds 2 Plus (5.5 h, maker figure) and just under the EarFun Air Pro 4 (6 h with LDAC and adaptive ANC, from Digital Trends). For someone who will actually use LDAC, the Liberty 4 NC's battery lead disappears, and it still wins on ANC alone (our page's SoundGuys score of 8.4 against 7.5 for the EarFun). The table's footnote would read: every headline battery figure is AAC at 50% volume, and LDAC cuts it by 40-55%.
